changelog: Insert a narrow fallback ordering rule in [Order Principles]: when two cuts lie in the same clause and one splits a verb (or verbal phrase) from its object/complement while the other completes the predicate, prefer the predicate-completing (later) cut. This addresses the primary finding (intra-clause verb-object splits) while scoping the preference to avoid removing early intra-clause options that short-latency budgets need.
findings: When two candidate cuts lie in the same clause, the prompt sometimes prefers an earlier intra-clause cut over the later cut that completes the clause's predicate, worsening cohesion.
The prompt permits cuts that split a verb (or verbal phrase) from the words that complete its object or complement, producing misleading or contradiction-prone preceding fragments.

diagnosis.why: The inserted fallback made the model prefer later intra-clause cuts that ‘complete the predicate’ (avoiding verb–object splits). That moved the rank-2 position up while slightly lowering rank-1, producing small gains for long-latency bins but removing many early intra-clause cut options that short-latency bins rely on, so harms concentrate in the short bins (notably ≤3/≤7) even though the overall mean is near zero.
diagnosis.lesson: Keep the predicate-completion preference narrowly scoped so it does not eliminate early intra-clause cut options that short-latency budgets need (i.e., avoid suppressing top-1 early cuts while promoting later predicate-completing cuts).
